To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oral administration of intestine-targeted zinc-pecitinate beads containing activated carbon (AC) can decrease intestinal ciprofloxacine residues and thus may reduce the emergence of ciprlofloxacin resistance.
zinc-pectinate activated charcoal beads can be used as a colon-targeted delivery system to reduce the amount of residual antibiotics reaching the colon.
intestine-targeted beads containing AC were able to decrease residual intestinal ciprofloxin in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an innovative drug delivery system for the inactivation and the elimination of residual antibiotics in the gastrointestinal tract.
the development of a new generation of beads able to reduce the risk of antibiotic resistance in the gastrointestinal system.
the use of AC loaded zinc pectinate beads as a potential tool to prevent the emergence of antibiotic resistances.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zinc-pectinate bead technology has the potential to reduce residual antibiotics in the gastrointestinal tract.
the intestine-targeted zinc-pecitinate beads loaded with AC are a promising tool for the prevention of antibiotic resistances.
the zinc pectinate beads loaded with activated carbon can be used for the removal of residual ciprofloxacine in the gastrointestinal tract and thus can prevent the selection of new resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of AC loaded zinc pectinate beads may be a promising strategy to decrease the residual fraction of antibiotics in the colon.
the intestinal microbiota is an important factor for the development of antibiotic resistance and that the use of colon-targeted AC-loaded zinc-pectinate could provide a better microbiota protection.
the intestinal microbiota is not only influenced by the amount of residual ciprofloxacine in the gut, but also by the location where the antibiotic is eliminated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have designed a new type of colon-targeted bead that could be used to decrease the intestinal residual ciproflovaxin fraction in the human gastrointestinal tract.
the use of AC in colon-targeted beads may be an interesting alternative for the removal of residual antibiotics in the colon.
the rat model does not seem to be a suitable model for the evaluation of colon-targeted beads.
